CSCI3100 Software Engineering

Introduction

Target: Learn how to blow water on the theory of software development.

Software Development Processes

Plan-and-Development: specification -> design -> implementation -> verification -> maintanence

Agile Manifesto: speed up life-cycles + interaction with users (user stories) + respond to change + test-driven development (TDD) (autotest) + behaviour-driven development (BDD) (cucumber)

Testing: for quality assurance (QA), verification (match spec?) + validation (spec correct?), unit -> module -> integration -> system testing

Productivity: clarity (conciseness) + synthesis (gen code by code) + reuse (Don't Repeat Yourself, DRY) + automation (use tools)

Software-as-a-Service (SaaS): Service-oriented architecture (SOA) and microservices (e.g. cloud computing or webpages) are popular.

Learning Languages and Frameworks

Steps: Type -> Primitive -> Method -> Class -> Symbols -> Library -> Debugging -> Testing

Ruby is weak-typing, everything is an object (only nil and false are falsy), where function calls are simply sending signals to the receiver. Sometimes {} and () are optional.

class A < B; @balance (instance variable); @@bank (class variable); balance (instance method); self.bank (class method); attr_accessor: (R+W) / attr_reader: (R) / attr_writer: (W)

Hashs: {:a => 1, :b => "two"}, :a are enumerables, f-string "Answer is #{@foo}" or %Q{Answer is #{@foo + 1}}

Lists: x.sort (include Comparable; <=>), x.reverse! (modifies), x.filter do |f| f.includes?("e") end, x.any? { |f| f.length > 5 }; yield and iterator

Library: gem, require "abc" then bundle install, specified in Gemfile (Gemfile.lock)

Software-as-a-Service (SaaS)

Client-Server Pattern: a server responds to many clients; Peer-to-Peer Architecture: everyone serves as client and server

HTTP is stateless and relies on TCP/IP protocols; Web 2.0 involves the introduction of javascript (Asynchonous JavaScript - AJAX and XmlHttpRequest).

RESTful API (REpresentational State Transfer): Represent requests to action on resources, which JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) are useful.

Sinatra: path /:user/account -> params[]; Views: .erb; erb :view; cookies: session[]

Model-View-Controller (MVC) Framework - Rails

Model: how data are stored and manipulated (CRUD); View: how to display data for users to interact; Controller: controller actions are generated in front-end and handled back-end

Rails's MVC: models/*.rb <-> controllers/*.rb (MoveController#show) <-> views/[action].html.erb. Routes: get '/movie/:id', debug(@movie)

Database: ApplicationRecord, Movie.where("rating = :rating", rating: 'PG'); new, save, save! (exception), update, destroy; Foreign key: has_many, belongs_to; scope for lambdas

Validation: validate :function or valid? Filters: before_action :function_name; Shared templates: <%= render "form", moviegoer: @moviegoer %>

Single Sign On (SSO): Third party login

Behaviour-Driven Design (BDD)

User Story: a "story" to verify if execute correctly (cucumber)

Feature: story name; Scenario: path; describe: context; Given [condition] When [do something] Then [check condition] And [condition] But [condition]

Capybara: visit; click_link; fill_in "xxx", :with => "yyy"; select "xxx" form "yyy"; click_button "xxx"; .find (with selenium)

Declarative Scenario: Given /I have added "(.*)" with rating "(.*)"/ do |title, rating|

Test-Driven Development (TDD)

RSpec: [precondition] act [assert]. expect(x).to eq('Ruby'); expect(res).to render_template("movies/search"); allow, double

Design Pattern

Single Responsibility Principle: Everything do one thing

Open/Closed Principle: Open for extension, closed for modification

Liskov Substitution Principle: Subtype can substitute base type

Injecting Dependency: create abstraction to reduce source modification

Demeter Principle: minimally expose yourself
